name: Am I The Only One Around Here
look: A still from The Big Lebowski. John Goodman as Walter Sobchak, a heavyset bearded man in tinted aviator glasses, a khaki vest and dark brown shirt, scowls and raises a black pistol beside his head in a bowling alley.
use: An exasperated rant about being the only person who cares about something. The top line reads 'Am I the only one around here' and the bottom finishes it with the rule, chore or courtesy everyone else ignores.
slots: top caption, usually 'Am I the only one around here'
bottom caption: the thing nobody else seems to care about
examples: Am I the only one around here
who refills the ice cube tray?
Am I the only one around here
who reads the group chat before asking what time we're meeting?
describe: angry guy in glasses holding up a gun at a bowling alley
big bearded man in aviator shades raising a pistol
john goodman with a handgun in the big lebowski
furious bowler in a vest waving a gun around
mad man pulls a gun over a bowling rule
origin: From The Big Lebowski (1998): Walter Sobchak pulls a gun on a fellow bowler over a foot foul, asking if he's the only one who cares about the rules.
